title: David Bowie's birth chart
metaDescription: David Bowie's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 17.4° Capricorn. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Sun and Mars sit 0.6° from an exact conjunction — near enough that the tradition reads identity and drive as a single working part. When two functions occupy one degree, the tradition reads a fusion: neither can act without committing the other.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun's exact place is 17.4° Capricorn. That falls in the second decan, 10°–20°, sub-ruled by Venus in the classical scheme — an earth sign read through a cardinal season.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: Mercury holds 8.4° Capricorn, Venus holds 2.3° Sagittarius, Mars holds 16.8° Capricorn — in the old shorthand, a mind that trusts the measured and the checked; taste that runs toward the vivid and the immediate; drive that grinds rather than flares.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The Sun and Mars hold the closest angle here — a conjunction, 0.6° wide. When two functions occupy one degree, the tradition reads a fusion: neither can act without committing the other. Behind it, Neptune sextile Pluto at 1.9°, and Mercury square Neptune at 2.4° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: Uranus stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The classical table has two entries for this chart. Mars in Capricorn at 16.8° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Saturn in Leo at 6.8° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain. The old table grades terrain, not talent — a placement in fall works uphill, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Counting only the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the chart runs 3 earth, 3 fire, 2 air, 1 water by element and 4 cardinal, 3 fixed, 2 mutable by modality. An earth emphasis reads as patience with material reality — slow hands, durable results. Saturn, Uranus and Pluto were retrograde — apparent retreat against the stars, which the old reading takes as a function working from the inside first.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Cancer into Leo during that day at the birthplace, travelling 15.0° between one midnight and the next. A birth time would settle it in a second; there isn’t one. So the Moon stays unnamed here — the alternative is a guess wearing the clothes of a fact.
